newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks advance in early trading.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks advance in early trading.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks advanced in early trading on Thursday morning on good turnover and bullish market sentiment buoyed by the Dow's record breaking performance, brokers said.
"Market sentiment is still bullish," said Ronald Lam, chief dealer at Dao Heng Securities. "The Dow's 16-point gain and new high has boosted Hong Kong sentiment."

The Hang Seng Index gained 7.57 points to 12,403.75 in the first 30 minutes of trade on turnover of HK$1.30 billion. The total was boosted by heavy trade in Consolidated Electric Power Asia shares, brokers said.
EPA was unchanged at HK$17.90 as shares worth HK$56.34 million were crossed in the market.
Southern Co has offered CEPA shareholders HK$18.50 in cash for their shares, payable in either one or two payments..
On Wednesday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 16 to 6021, topping the previous record closing high of 6,010.00 set on Monday.
He added that few investors in Hong Kong wanted to sell the market since there was no other Asian market performing as well to shift funds into.
The market rose 111 points in early Wednesday trading, then dropped 95 points in the afternoon on rumours of rights issues and futures-related selling, brokers said.
"The market was led by futures trading yesterday, that will dictate the direction's today," said Adam Conn at HSBC James Capel Asia.
The October Hang Seng Index futures contract fell 32 points to 12,380 in early trade.
Sun Hung Kai and Co resumed trading. The share dipped HK$0.30 to HK$2.10.
The company announced a two-for-five rights issue at HK$1.80 per rights share, aimed at raising about HK$498 million to be used to reduce debt and as working capital.
First Pacific denied on Wednesday rumours that the company was planning a rights issue. The share was one of the most active on Thursday, rising HK$0.30 to HK$11.10.
